question: Where did the PIL come into being? (RPF Constable 2018 (24/01/2019) Shift 3)
options: England
United States of America
Russia
Ireland
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is United States of America

Explanation:
PIL (Public Interest Litigation) originated in the United States of America. The concept developed during the 1960s and 1970s through civil rights movements and environmental protection lawsuits. In India, the Supreme Court adopted PIL in the 1980s, with Justices P.N. Bhagwati and V.R. Krishna Iyer playing a pivotal role. The aim is to provide access to justice for disadvantaged groups.

☛ Other term used for PIL → Social interest litigation

question_hi: PIL का उदय कहाँ हुआ? (RPF Constable 2018 (24/01/2019) Shift 3)

आयरलैंड

Solution: सही उत्तर है संयुक्त राज्य अमेरिका

Explanation:
PIL (Pubic Interest Litigation) का उदय संयुक्त राज्य अमेरिका में हुआ। यह अवधारणा 1960-70 के दशक में नागरिक अधिकार आंदोलनों और पर्यावरण संरक्षण से जुड़े मुकदमों के माध्यम से विकसित हुई। भारत में PIL को सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने 1980 के दशक में अपनाया, जिसमें न्यायमूर्ति पी.एन. भगवती और न्यायमूर्ति वी.आर. कृष्णा अय्यर ने महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाई। PIL का उद्देश्य समाज के कमजोर वर्गों तक न्याय पहुंचाना है।

question: According to the Constitution, how much is the number of members in the Rajya Sabha? (RPF Constable 2018 (24/01/2019) Shift 3)
options: 250 Members
240 Members
245 Members
260 Members
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 250 Members

Explanation:
According to Article 80 of the Indian Constitution, the maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha is fixed at 250 members. Out of these, 238 members are elected representatives of states and union territories, while 12 members are nominated by the President. These nominated members are individuals having special knowledge or practical experience in fields such as literature, art, science, and social service. Currently, the actual strength of the Rajya Sabha is 245 members, but the constitutional provision allows a maximum of 250. Rajya Sabha is a permanent house and its members have a term of 6 years.

question: In 1947, who coined the word of judicial activism? (RPF Constable 2018 (24/01/2019) Shift 3)
options: Gold Singh
Balwant Roy Mehta -
Arthur Sleddinger
Munro
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Arthur Sleddinger

Explanation:
The term judicial activism was coined in 1947 by American historian Arthur Sleddinger. It refers to the proactive role of the judiciary in reviewing government policies and protecting citizens' rights. In India, judicial activism has led to landmark judgments, including the development of the basic structure doctrine in the Kesavananda Bharati case. While the term originated in the US context, it has significantly influenced the Indian legal system, empowering courts to intervene in matters of public interest through writ petitions under Articles 32 and 226 of the Constitution. This doctrine emphasizes the judiciary's duty to uphold constitutional values and ensure justice.

☛ Judicial activism meaning → Active role of judiciary in policy review
☛ Basis of judicial activism in India → Articles 32 and 226 of Constitution
☛ Basic structure doctrine → Developed in Kesavananda Bharati case
☛ Purpose of judicial activism → Protection of citizens' rights

question: In what year was the Election Commission of India established? (RPF Constable 2018 (24/01/2019) Shift 3)
options: 1956
1950
1955
1960
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1950

Explanation:
The Election Commission of India was established on January 25, 1950, a day before the Constitution came into effect. It is an independent constitutional body responsible for conducting and regulating elections in India. It derives its powers from Article 324 of the Constitution. The first Chief Election Commissioner was Sukumar Sen. Its headquarters is located in New Delhi. The first general elections were held in 1952. The commission ensures free and fair elections.

question: The Lok Sabha is also known as _____. (RPF Constable 2018 (24/01/2019) Shift 3)
options: General House
House of the People
House of Lords
House of Representatives
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is House of the People

Explanation:
The Lok Sabha is the lower house of the Indian Parliament, known as the House of the People because its members are directly elected by the citizens of India. According to Article 81 of the Constitution, the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha is 552 members, of which 530 represent states, 20 represent union territories, and 2 were earlier nominated by the President from the Anglo-Indian community (this provision has been abolished). The normal term of the Lok Sabha is 5 years, but the President can dissolve it earlier. The presiding officer of the Lok Sabha is called the Speaker.

question: How is the minimum age for becoming a member of the Rajya Sabha? (RPF Constable 2018 (24/01/2019) Shift 3)

40 years

35 years
solution:

Explanation:
According to Article 84(b) of the Indian Constitution, the minimum age to become a member of the Rajya Sabha is 30 years. This is higher than the minimum age of 25 years for the Lok Sabha, as the Rajya Sabha is designed to be a house of more experienced and mature members. question_hi: राज्यसभा का सदस्य बनने की न्यूनतम आयु क्या है? (RPF Constable 2018 (24/01/2019) Shift 3)

question: Who were the pioneers of the concept of PIL in India? (RPF Constable 2018 (24/01/2019) Shift 3)
options: Justice V. R. Krishna Iyer and P. Sathasivam
Justice P. N. Bhagwati and A. N. Ray
Justice P. Sadashivam and P.N. Bhagwati
Justice V. R. Krishna Iyer and P.N. Bhagwati
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Justice V. R. Krishna Iyer and P.N. Bhagwati

Explanation:
The pioneers of the concept of Public Interest Litigation (PIL) in India are Justice V. R. Krishna Iyer and Justice P. N. Bhagwati. They promoted PIL during the 1970s and 1980s through judicial activism. Justice Bhagwati opened the doors of the Supreme Court for PIL, enabling marginalized groups to access justice. Justice Iyer also established PIL principles in several landmark judgments. PIL aims to ensure judicial intervention in public issues, especially when the vulnerable are affected.

question: How many sessions are there in a year in Parliament? (RPF Constable 2018 (24/01/2019) Shift 3)

5 sessions
2 sessions
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 3 sessions

Explanation:
The Indian Parliament holds three sessions in a year: Budget Session, Monsoon Session, and Winter Session. The Budget Session is from February to May, the Monsoon Session from July to September, and the Winter Session from November to December. The duration of each session is not fixed and is decided by the government. The Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs plans these sessions. The President addresses both houses at the beginning of each session. The Budget Session is the most important session as the Union Budget is presented during it. Each session has multiple sittings, and the government can also call a special session if needed.

question: Which of the following determines whether a member of the Lok Sabha is disqualified or not? (RPF Constable 2018 (25/01/2019) Shift 1)
options: Speaker
Vice President
Prime
Chief Minister
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Speaker

Explanation:
The Speaker of Lok Sabha determines whether a member of the Lok Sabha is disqualified. This is provided in Article 103 of the Indian Constitution, which makes the Speaker or Chairman the final authority in matters related to disqualification of members. Although the President may be consulted, the decision rests with the Speaker. Grounds for disqualification include defection under the Anti-Defection Law (10th Schedule), holding an office of profit, or other legal disqualifications. The Vice President is the Chairman of Rajya Sabha, while the Prime Minister and Chief Minister are executive heads and have no role in this decision.

question: Part II of Indian Constitution is associated with                  . (RPF Constable 2018 (25/01/2019) Shift 1)
options: Citizenship
Basic Duties
Elections
Basic Rights
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Citizenship

Explanation:
Part II of the Indian Constitution (Articles 5-11) deals with Citizenship. It defines citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution, rights of citizenship, and the rights of foreign citizens. Articles 5 to 8 grant citizenship to persons born in India, of Indian parentage, or those who migrated from Pakistan. Article 9 terminates Indian citizenship if a person voluntarily acquires citizenship of another country. Article 10 ensures the continuation of citizenship rights, while Article 11 empowers Parliament to regulate citizenship by law. This part forms the basis of the Citizenship Act, 1955, which further elaborates on the acquisition and termination of citizenship. The provisions ensure clarity on who is a citizen of India at the start and how future citizenship matters will be handled.

question: Who is appointed for the discharge of his post in that state when the post of the governor of a state dies during his tenure? (RPF Constable 2018 (25/01/2019) Shift 3)
options: State Advocate General
Chief Minister
Chief Justice of the High Courts of the respective states
Interim Deputy Governor
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Chief Justice of the High Courts of the respective states

Explanation:
According to Article 153 of the Indian Constitution, in the event of the death or absence of a Governor, the Chief Justice of the High Court of that state discharges the functions of the Governor. This provision is outlined in Article 160, which empowers the President to make temporary arrangements. This arrangement continues until a new Governor is appointed. The Chief Justice is authorized to act as an interim Governor. This system ensures continuity in state administration. In case of the Governor's death, neither the Deputy Governor nor the Chief Minister but the Chief Justice of the High Court is entrusted with this responsibility.

question: Special provisions relating to Delhi have been given under which article of the Constitution? (RPF Constable 2018 (25/01/2019) Shift 3)
options: Article 262
Article 239
Article 242
Article 240
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 239

Explanation:
Under Article 239 of the Constitution, special provisions are made for Union Territories, including Delhi. This article empowers the President to appoint an Administrator for each Union Territory. Delhi was given a special status with a Legislative Assembly and Council of Ministers through the 69th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1991, which inserted Articles 239AA and 239AB. Article 262 deals with inter-state water disputes, Article 242 has been repealed, and Article 240 empowers the President to make regulations for certain Union Territories. Thus, the foundational special provision for Delhi is contained in Article 239.

question_hi: संविधान के किस अनुच्छेद के तहत दिल्ली से संबंधित विशेष प्रावधान दिए गए हैं? (RPF Constable 2018 (25/01/2019) Shift 3)
